tasks.title: Real-corpus coi-screen validation (~814K ICIJ): exercise mmap end-to-end + answer B-1 (is full-graph enumeration a hot path?)
Harden the JSON<->mmap equivalence oracle to property-based/fuzzed coverage (precondition for mmap-default in v1.2)
OpenTelemetry tracing + SLO/SLI docs (additive; pairs with existing Prometheus metrics)
Re-enable the disabled fuzz tests (pkg/api/fuzz_test.go.disabled, pkg/query/fuzz_test.go.disabled)
CI: repo-wide gofmt -s lint gate. ROADMAP v1.3 says not started, but #490 added the gofmt -s step to test.yml and .golangci.yml sets gofmt.simplify
GraphQL index-level pagination: resolver offset -> ID cursor (REST side landed in #366)
F3 compliance HTTP-API surface over the existing pkg/compliance framework (endpoints only) — already shipped May 2026 (#111/#114/#122/#124); re-listed in error, closed 2026-09-11 with PR 124
SDK parity: Python, TypeScript and Go clients catch up to the v1.4 endpoints

Real-corpus coi-screen run (Milestone-1-proper, ~814K ICIJ). Needs the sibling coi-screen repo checked out beside graphdb and an ICIJ corpus on the machine; runbook in SPIKE_COI_SCREEN_VALIDATION_2026-07-01.md

storage: Close must not rewrite the snapshot when the session wrote nothing. Surfaced by v1.1-coi-screen-real-corpus (#594): a read-only consumer rewrites the 1.1 GB snapshot.mmap on every exit (8.3 s / 7.9 GB; JSON 25 s / 17.5 GB). Acceptance: mtime and bytes unchanged after a read-only open/close, changed after one write, both seen red first; WAL truncate stays tied to a snapshot that happened. Spec row in NEXT_STEPS_2026-06-18.md section D

storage: JSON-mode Close must not rewrite snapshot.json when the session wrote nothing. Same defect as v1.4-close-no-rewrite-when-clean (#598) on the other representation: a read-only consumer pays 25 s / 17.5 GB per exit on the 2.0M-node ICIJ store. JSON has no overlay, so the proof differs: WAL empty at open and LSN unchanged since, plus every unlogged mutation path (index definitions, SetEncryption, DeleteAllNodes) accounted for. BulkImportMode has no WAL and must always write. Acceptance: snapshot.json mtime and bytes unchanged after a read-only open/close, changed after one write, both seen red first; WAL truncate stays tied to a snapshot that happened

storage: a WAL append failure must not be reported to the caller as success. Today enqueueWAL (9 sites, node and edge ops), waitWALPending (14 sites) and writeToWAL (6 sites, property and vector index definitions) print to stderr and return nil; the in-memory mutation stays, the WAL entry is missing, and until #602 Close could drop it. Decide and implement one contract: the caller gets an error and the in-memory change is rolled back, or the store refuses further writes until a snapshot lands. Acceptance: with a write fault on the WAL file, no public write method returns nil; a test per path family, each seen red first; replay after a crash never lacks a write the API confirmed. Interface change: propose the contract to the user before code

api,graphql: map storage.ErrWALWriteFailed to a response that stops a client retry. Since v1.4-wal-write-errors-reach-the-caller a single-op write returns ErrWALWriteFailed with the entity applied in memory; the REST and GraphQL handlers surface it as a generic error, and a client that retries creates a second node. Acceptance: the REST status and body and the GraphQL error extension say the write applied and must not be retried, and carry the entity ID; one handler test per surface, each seen red first

storage: a snapshot records the WAL boundary LSN it covers, and replay skips entries at or below it. Today a Close whose snapshot lands but whose WAL truncate fails for any cause (disk error at exit) leaves entries the snapshot already holds, and the next open replays them: a create from before a delete resurrects the deleted entity. Additive field in the JSON snapshot and in the mmap metadata tail (no version bump needed if absent means 0); replay compares entry.LSN to it. Acceptance: with the truncate forced to fail after a successful snapshot, a deleted node stays deleted after reopen, on both formats, seen red first

ci,scripts: run the local go test gate inside a private network namespace so Portmaster cannot drop loopback SYNs. Signature: pkg/auth/oidc TestOIDCHandler_Callback_Success timed out at 136 s on a loopback connect under go test ./pkg/... and passed alone. Reuse in_private_netns and netns_available from graphdb-coord scripts/lib/netns.sh (PR #45 there). Acceptance: with portmaster.service active, a closed loopback port is refused in under 1 s inside the wrapper; the gate runs green with zero dial timeouts; when unshare is refused the gate takes a WARN fallback and still runs the tests

go-client: do not retry POST or PATCH on a 5xx (M-11 parity with the TS and Python clients); read the 202 applied-not-durable body from v1.4-api-wal-error-no-retry and return a typed ErrNotDurable with the entity id. Today clients/go/transport.go isRetryable is 429 or >= 500 and request() retries with no method check, default 2 retries, so a POST /nodes that fails after the write applied creates a second node

storage: refuse the open when the recovered WAL LSN is above 0 and below the recorded snapshot boundary (a downgrade to a binary that resets the LSN wrote entries the skip would drop); a failed truncate gives recovered == boundary and never fires; decide what to do about a torn WAL tail that reads low; red first with the measured sequence

ts-client: a 202 applied-not-durable response is not a success. Today the TypeScript client returns the body as a normal result and drops the applied and durable fields, so the caller cannot tell a durable write from one that only applied in memory. Same shape as #618 for the Go client: read the 202 body, return a typed NotDurableError that carries the entity id, and never retry it. Acceptance: one test per write method family sees the typed error on a 202, each seen red first; a 201 path is unchanged

python-client: a 202 applied-not-durable response is not a success. Today the Python client returns the body as a normal result and drops the applied and durable fields, so the caller cannot tell a durable write from one that only applied in memory. Same shape as #618 for the Go client: read the 202 body, raise a typed NotDurableError that carries the entity id, and never retry it. Acceptance: one test per write method family sees the typed error on a 202, each seen red first; a 201 path is unchanged

storage,docs: decide the contract for a WAL backend switch on one data directory. Since #619 the open refuses, which is loud, but no repair or migration path exists. Decide with the user whether the refusal is the documented contract or a migration is necessary. Acceptance: either docs name the refusal, its error, and the operator repair steps, or a migration opens the directory after a switch with a test seen red first. Small: docs or code

storage: poison the WAL after a sync failure. Today a sync failure leaves the LSN counter advanced while the bytes may not be durable, so the recorded snapshot boundary can exceed the durable LSN and a later open refuses with ErrWALBehindSnapshot (#619 residual). Decision: after a sync failure every later Append returns an error; Close still writes the snapshot and truncates the WAL, so no LSN is reused and the boundary never runs ahead of durable bytes. Acceptance: force a sync failure after a successful flush, then append (error), close, reopen (opens clean), seen red first

scripts: consumer-drive.sh SKIP policy. On a SKIP the script prints a warning and exits 0 when CI is unset, and exits 1 when CI=true, so a local run stays usable and a CI run cannot pass on a skipped drive. Small, scripts only. Acceptance: a selftest shows the exit 1 under CI=true and the exit 0 without it, seen red first

api: decide one storage rule for string property values. A REST write (POST/PUT /nodes, /edges, batch) stores html.EscapeString text (pkg/storage/sanitizer.go:24, called from pkg/api/handler_helper.go:300). A bound Cypher write stores raw text (pkg/api/server_handlers.go:173). Reads do not decode, so CONTAINS matches entity text. Ulysses encodes on write and decodes on read to match; a change must ship with the Ulysses client in the same release, and Ulysses must hear first. Acceptance: one documented rule, a consumer contract that pins it, a note for data already stored encoded, seen red first

api: a JSON null in PUT /nodes/{id} and PUT /edges/{id} removes the key (JSON Merge Patch, RFC 7396). Ulysses priority 1 of 5: its mappers omit a cleared field and PUT merges, so a cleared value stays in the graph. Today a null is stored as a TypeJSON null (pkg/storage/value_from_json.go), UpdateNode (node_operations.go:522) and UpdateEdge (edge_operations.go:350) only merge, and only nodes have a removal path (RemoveNodeProperties, node_operations.go:605, via Cypher REMOVE). Lines read at ac4f79f. Decide what a null does on create. Ulysses writes metadata null on its create paths and reads a missing key as {}. Visible change: tell ulysses-d4 the release that ships it. Acceptance: a consumer contract for nodes and edges, the vector entry removed with the key, seen red first

algorithms: label propagation reads the edges of every node again in each iteration. Build the neighbour lists once for each run. Ulysses priority 2 of 5, performance only. Both versions do it: labelPropagationView (pkg/algorithms/community_tenant.go:59, loop at :69, neighbours at :44) and LabelPropagation (community_propagation.go:25). Lines read at ac4f79f. Acceptance: the same communities on the existing tests, a benchmark before and after

storage: CreateVectorIndexForTenant (pkg/storage/vector_operations.go:123) builds an empty index, so a node written before the index exists joins it only at the next open (rebuildVectorIndexesFromNodes, :352). Insert the existing vectors at create time. Ulysses priority 3 of 5, additive. Lines read at ac4f79f. Acceptance: a node created before the index is found by a search right after the create, seen red first

api: /traverse sends X-Truncated (handlers_algorithms_traversal.go:106) and /query sends X-Traversal-Truncated. Send X-Traversal-Truncated from /traverse as well and keep X-Truncated as an alias. Ulysses priority 4 of 5. Ulysses reads X-Truncated on /traverse, so do not remove it without telling ulysses-d4 first. Lines read at ac4f79f. Acceptance: CC22 pins both names

query: the query-text sanitizer (pkg/query/sanitizer.go) refuses data: and file: (:36, :38) and collapses whitespace (:76) over the whole text, string literals included. Run both on non-literal tokens only, so a literal keeps its exact text. Ulysses priority 5 of 5: it binds every string and gets nothing from this. Lines read at ac4f79f. Acceptance: a literal with file: and two spaces comes back byte for byte, the refusal still fires outside a literal, seen red first

query: a Cypher write stores any value that is not a string, int, float or bool as its Go %v text with TypeString, and answers 200 with no error. Probed through REST /query at 7c6705c: SET n.x = null and SET n.x = $v with v null both store the string <nil>, a bound list stores [a b], a bound map stores map[k:1]; a string control stores correctly. Cause: the default branch of convertToStorageValue (pkg/query/executor_steps.go:65-66, read at 7c6705c) runs StringValue(fmt.Sprintf(%v)). It has 8 callers, the SET paths and the MATCH and MERGE property comparisons (physical_ops_scan.go:277, physical_ops_mutate.go:313). REST already converts through storage.ValueFromJSON. Likely fix: route the default branch through ValueFromJSON so Cypher and REST store the same value. Decide null: Cypher semantics say SET n.x = null removes the key, which also matches PUT after #634 (the lean), or store a JSON null as REST POST does. CREATE with null was not measured. Acceptance: null, list and map round-trip on SET, CREATE and a MATCH comparison, seen red first

storage: add UpsertNodeForTenant(tenantID, labels, properties, keyLabel, keyProperty) (node, created, err) and UpsertNodeWithUniquenessRulesForTenant(tenantID, labels, properties), the node twin of UpsertEdgeWithTenant (pkg/storage/edge_operations.go:635). Find and create in one gs.mu hold, as CreateNodeWithUniquePropertyForTenant (node_operations.go:134). On a match: new properties override, absent ones stay, labels do not change. More than one match is an error, never a silent choice. Asked by mapper-6b (oit-cyber/mapper, embeds pkg/storage). Lines read at 5988924. Acceptance: concurrent upserts of one key make one node, the duplicate case errors, seen red first

api: an atomic upsert on POST /nodes and POST /nodes/batch (flag, for example on_conflict=merge), keyed by the registered uniqueness rule for the labels (option B, as POST /nodes already routes through CreateNodeWithUniquenessRulesForTenant, handlers_nodes.go:143). 201 on create, 200 on match, 400 when no rule matches. Needed by mapper team mode, where two assessors ingest one host at the same time. Lines read at 5988924. Acceptance: two concurrent requests for one key give one node and one 201, seen red first

clients/go: Nodes.Upsert and Nodes.BatchUpsert over the REST upsert, returning the node and a created flag. The client has no node or edge upsert today (clients/go/edges.go). For mapper team mode. Acceptance: client tests cover created true, created false and the no-rule 400

api: the 409 from POST /nodes on a uniqueness conflict (handlers_nodes.go:160-162) names the existing node only in the error text (UniqueConstraintError.Error, pkg/storage/errors.go:168). Add a structured conflicting_node_id field to the body and expose it on the Go client Error. mapper uses 409 then a lookup until this lands. Lines read at 5988924. Acceptance: the field equals the node that holds the key, seen red first

query: Cypher MERGE discards UpdateNodeForTenant errors with _ = on ON MATCH and ON CREATE (pkg/query/physical_ops_mutate.go:344, :377) and then writes the value into the returned node anyway, so a failed update returns 200 and a row that the store does not hold. Return the error and do not change the row. Found by mapper-6b. Lines read at 5988924. Acceptance: a failing update (for example a closed store or a WAL failure) surfaces from MERGE, seen red first

storage: nothing stops two processes opening one data directory (a word search for flock in pkg and cmd finds 0). Take flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on <DataDir>/LOCK at open, hold it until Close, refuse with a typed error naming the directory. Not fcntl (released by any close in-process) and not a PID file (stale after a crash). Unix build tags. Sweep tests that open one directory twice without Close. Asked by mapper-6b: a server and an embedded mapper can share a laptop. Lines read at 5988924. Acceptance: a second open of a held directory refuses, a reopen after Close succeeds, seen red first

storage: CreateNodeWithUniquePropertyForTenant scans every node of the label under gs.mu (membershipNodeIDsByLabelLocked, node_operations.go:163), so N unique creates cost O(N^2). Use the property index when one exists on the key. The index is global per key (index_operations.go:119), so filter by tenant and label. It holds only values of its own type (:26), so keep the scan for other types. Prove the index covers mmap base records after reopen. Wait for the mapper-6b /16 spike numbers before sizing. Lines read at 5988924. Acceptance: a teeth test that removes an index entry makes the check fail, seen red first

query: MATCH (a:P)-[:R]->(b:Q) WHERE a.pid = 1 RETURN b.name returns x with no index and null once a property index exists on pid. The optimizer swaps the whole MatchStep for an IndexLookupStep (pkg/query/optimizer.go:97) without checking for relationships, so the expansion is lost. Creating an index changes query results. Probed at 5988924 (scratchpad zz_gap_probe_test.go.keep). Acceptance: same rows with and without the index, seen red first

query: with a property index, MATCH (p) WHERE p.indexed = 1 AND p.other > 5 DELETE p deletes the node when the second condition is false, because applyFilterPushdown puts the FilterStep after the write step when the MatchStep became an IndexLookupStep

query: MATCH ()-[r:R]->() DELETE r answers affected=1 and leaves the edge in storage. DeleteStep.deleteVariable returns nil for anything that is not a node (pkg/query/executor_steps.go:386-388). Probed at 5988924. Acceptance: the edge is gone from storage after DELETE r, and an unsupported binding type refuses instead of skipping, seen red first

query: MATCH ()-[r:R]->() SET r.w = 5 answers affected=1 and writes nothing; the stored edge has no properties. SetStep.executeAssignment returns nil for anything that is not a node (pkg/query/executor_steps.go:270-272). Probed at 5988924. Acceptance: SET and REMOVE on an edge property persist (read back from storage), seen red first

query: MATCH (a:P) MATCH (b:Q) RETURN a.pid, b.name returns a.pid = null. The parser keeps one slot per clause (pkg/query/parser.go:64 query.Match = matchClause), so a second MATCH, SET or MERGE replaces the first, and buildExecutionPlan (executor_plan.go:177) runs clauses in a fixed order, not text order. Probed at 5988924. Acceptance: either both MATCH clauses bind, or the parser refuses a repeated clause; never a silent drop. Seen red first

query: MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.city, count(n) over cities A, A, B returns 3 rows with count = null instead of 2 grouped rows. Grouping only happens with the non-Cypher GROUP BY (pkg/query/executor_results.go:55). openCypher groups by every non-aggregate RETURN item. Probed at 5988924. Acceptance: (A, 2) and (B, 1), GROUP BY keeps working, seen red first

query: plain DELETE of a node that has edges deletes the node and its edges with no error (DeleteStep ignores Detach and calls DeleteNodeForTenant, pkg/query/executor_steps.go:379-395). Neo4j refuses this unless the query says DETACH DELETE. Decide: refuse (openCypher) or document the divergence; refusing may break a consumer, so check docs/CONSUMER_CONTRACTS.md first. Probed at 5988924

api: the /health/ready storage check always passes; it calls graph.GetStatistics() and returns nil (pkg/api/server_init.go:181-184). A poisoned WAL (#624) or a closed store is invisible to a load balancer or orchestrator. Report not-ready when the WAL is poisoned or the store is closed. Read at 5988924. Acceptance: readiness goes 503 after a forced WAL sync failure, seen red first

tenant: quotas are stored and shown but never enforced. CheckNodeQuota and CheckEdgeQuota (pkg/tenant/store.go:381, :403) have no caller outside pkg/tenant. Wire them into the node and edge create paths, enforcing only when a quota is set so an unset quota keeps today's behaviour. Read at 5988924. Acceptance: a create past the quota refuses with a typed error and HTTP 429 or 403, seen red first

storage: Batch.Commit returns at the first failing op and keeps every earlier op, in memory and in the WAL (each op calls appendToWAL alone, pkg/storage/batch_executor.go:110-380; early return at :40-42). The same return skips the vector inserts and observer notifications of the ops already applied. Callers are cmd/import-dimacs and cmd/import-icij. Make it all-or-nothing (one appendWALBatch, as Transaction.Commit does) or document and test partial semantics; do not leave vector state behind. Read at 5988924

api + clients: storage has UpsertEdgeWithTenant (pkg/storage/edge_operations.go:635) but REST has no route and no client has an edge upsert. Add it beside the node upsert flag (v1.4-rest-upsert-node) with the same 201/200 created signal, plus Go, TS and Python client functions. Read at 5988924

storage + api + query: a node's labels cannot change after create. No storage method adds or removes a label; PUT /nodes/{id} patches properties only (pkg/api/handlers_nodes.go:248); Cypher SET n:L and REMOVE n:L fail to parse because both parsers expect a dot (pkg/query/parser_clauses.go:280, :332). Add AddNodeLabelsForTenant and RemoveNodeLabelsForTenant that keep the label, tenant and membership indexes, the WAL and the uniqueness rules consistent. Read at 5988924. Acceptance: invariants pass after label changes on JSON and mmap reopen

storage + api: every node and edge write is last-writer-wins. Node and Edge have no version (pkg/storage/types.go:437) and REST has no ETag or If-Match. Design a version field (on-disk format impact: both snapshot formats need a version bump or an additive field) and a conditional update that refuses a stale write with 412. Design task first; read at 5988924

api: no REST route lists a tenant's labels, edge types or property keys. Storage has GetLabelsForTenant and GetEdgeTypesForTenant (pkg/storage/tenant_operations.go:516, :525) but nothing lists property keys. Add a read-only schema route that also lists property indexes, vector indexes and uniqueness rules. Read at 5988924

api: property indexes can only be created or dropped through the storage API (CreatePropertyIndex, DropPropertyIndex, pkg/storage/index_operations.go:10, :58). Add REST routes and client functions. An unmerged branch, origin/feat/expose-property-indexes-and-uniqueness (2026-05-24), did this before ADR 0001; check it before starting. Read at 5988924

api: POST has no Idempotency-Key. After a timeout a client cannot know whether its POST applied, so a manual retry can duplicate a node. The Go client never retries POST (clients/go/graphdb.go:4-5), so this is not an automatic duplicate. Add an optional Idempotency-Key header with a bounded server-side record. Read at 5988924

storage: the per-write fsync default (DefaultStorageConfig, pkg/storage/storage.go:24-33) was justified by BenchmarkWALFlushInterval numbers that reproduce exactly on tmpfs: b.TempDir() is /tmp, and /tmp is tmpfs on the dev box. Same binary, only TMPDIR changed, 32 writers, 5988924: tmpfs per-write 8 us/op vs batched-1ms 138 us/op; LUKS ext4 19,520 vs 2,794; plain btrfs NVMe 36,004 vs 4,996. Batched is about 7x faster on real disks. Make the benchmark refuse tmpfs (or take a data-dir variable and print the filesystem), add a single sequential writer case (batched adds up to one flush interval per write there), measure on real disks, fix the comment, then put the default decision to the user with numbers. Durability is the same in both modes. Found from a mapper-6b bulk-ingest spike on dm-crypt (about 20 KB/s WAL)

storage: CreateNodesWithTenant and CreateEdgesWithTenant on the default synchronous WAL write and fsync each record alone (createNodeLocked in a loop, pkg/storage/node_operations.go:67-90), so a 1,000-node call costs 1,000 fsyncs. Write the call as one WAL group with one fsync (appendWALBatch, as Transaction.Commit does), the Postgres COPY shape. Keep the documented partial-on-error contract or change it deliberately with v1.4-storage-batch-atomic-commit. The REST batch handlers loop single creates (handlers_nodes.go handleBatchNodes) and gain nothing unless they move to the bulk call; CC7 and CC20 pin their partial-success shape. Read at 5988924. Acceptance: fsync count per bulk call is 1 on the sync WAL, crash replay is all-or-nothing for the group, seen red first

storage: a BulkImportMode open skips WAL creation (pkg/storage/storage.go:138) and therefore replay (persistence_replay.go:13-30 returns nil with no WAL object), so WAL entries from a session that never closed are ignored. Probed at 5988924 with a sync-WAL store: a normal session created A (id 1) and stopped without Close; the bulk open saw 0 nodes and gave a new node B id 1; after the bulk Close a normal reopen held only B. A durable, acknowledged write was lost with no error, and CheckInvariants reported clean. Fix (user decision 2026-10-08): the bulk-mode open refuses with a typed error naming the data directory when the WAL holds entries past the snapshot boundary, and tells the operator to open in normal mode and Close first. Reported to mapper-6b (oit-cyber/mapper), which now uses bulk mode only on an empty directory. Acceptance: the probe sequence refuses at the bulk open and A survives, an empty or fully checkpointed WAL still opens in bulk mode, seen red first

storage: Value.AsInt, AsFloat and AsTimestamp read 8 bytes of v.Data and AsBool reads Data[0] with no length check (pkg/storage/types.go:201, :208, :222, :215), so a short or empty value panics: a Value{Type: TypeTimestamp} with 2 data bytes gives index out of range [7] with length 2. A damaged snapshot record or a Value built in Go code reaches them; the array decoders and AsVector already check. Return an error instead. Found by mapper-6b (TestFromValueRejectsForeignTypes). Read at e3e49e1. Acceptance: each scalar decoder errors on short and empty data, seen red first

storage: patchNode took a shard lock with no defer (pkg/storage/node_operations.go, lockShard before the property writes), so the nil-map panic fixed in #646 left the shard locked. The Cypher executor and net/http both recover a panic, so the store kept running with that shard held: later reads of it and Close waited forever (seen by mapper-6b as a test that hung to its timeout). Audit the write paths for locks released without defer and make each one panic-safe, or show why a panic cannot occur while it is held. Read at e3e49e1. Acceptance: a test that injects a panic under each audited lock and then calls Close returns, seen red first

storage: TypeTimestamp keeps whole Unix seconds (TimestampValue stores uint64(t.Unix()), AsTimestamp returns time.Unix(sec, 0) in the local zone; pkg/storage/types.go:93-97, :218-223), so time.Now() loses its sub-second part with no error. Existing stores hold 8-byte seconds, so sub-second precision needs a new value type or a format version: design first (on-disk impact, REST and GraphQL encoding, index ordering across the two types). Raised by mapper-6b, which now documents whole seconds UTC. Read at e3e49e1

storage: the mmap snapshot encoder writes property count, key length, tenant ID length, label count and label length as uint16 (pkg/storage/mmap_snapshot_format.go, the AppendUint16 calls in the node and edge record encoders), so a larger value wraps with no error. Probed at 07feb22 in the default mmap mode: a node with a 70,000-byte property key, or a 70,000-byte label, was created and closed with no error, and after reopen GetNode returned record unreadable: record did not decode. Fix (user decision 2026-10-08, ship in v1.6.0): refuse at create and update, in both snapshot modes, a key, label or tenant ID over 65,535 bytes and over 65,535 properties or labels, with a typed error (REST 400); and make the encoder return an error instead of wrapping, so an existing JSON store holding such data fails loudly on its first mmap Close. Edge type length too if the edge encoder narrows it. Found by a review of mapper-6b's embedded backend. Acceptance: the probe refuses at create, a direct encoder call with an oversize record errors, the 65,535 boundary still round-trips, seen red first

contracts: pin the six pkg/storage behaviours mapper (oit-cyber/mapper, embedded backend) depends on as CONSUMER CONTRACT tests and docs/CONSUMER_CONTRACTS.md rows (user decision 2026-10-08): (1) CreateNodesWithTenant/CreateEdgesWithTenant give each record a unique non-zero ID, (2) GetNodeForTenant errors with ErrNodeNotFound for an unknown or cross-tenant ID, (3) Get{Outgoing,Incoming}EdgesForTenant return an empty list and no error for an unknown node, (4) PatchNodeForTenant adds, changes and keeps keys, (5) BulkImportMode Close then a normal open reads all data, in mmap and JSON mode, (6) TimestampValue/AsTimestamp keep whole Unix seconds. A review at v1.5.0 found no test for (3), none for unique IDs in (1), none for a changed key in (4), and JSON-only coverage for (5). Note the library API is outside docs/STABILITY_POLICY.md; the rows record that graphdb tests these, not a versioned promise. Each test seen red against a deliberately broken variant

storage: with an EncryptionEngine set, rules.json (the uniqueness-rule registry, ADR 0001) is written in plaintext: pkg/storage/uniqueness_rules.go writes json.Marshal output and a rename with no encryption. A probe at 82efd5c with UseMmapSnapshot=false found a registered rule's label and property key in rules.json and in a backup archive, while snapshot.json and the WAL held no marker. Only schema names leak, not values, but an encrypted store should hold no plaintext it can avoid. Encrypt the file with the store's engine (rules.json has its own version field, so this needs a version bump and a read path for the old plaintext form), or document it as plaintext by design. Found by the encryption review for mapper-6b. Acceptance: the whole-directory marker test (v1.4-encryption-no-plaintext-test) finds no rule name in rules.json, seen red first

test: TestSnapshot_EncryptedEnvelopeFlagAndOpaquePayload (pkg/storage/snapshot_envelope_test.go:103) checks that an encrypted snapshot does not contain the raw text envelope-roundtrip. A property value is a []byte, and JSON encodes it as base64, so the raw text never appears even in a plaintext snapshot: a control by the reviewer found the raw search false and the base64 search true on a plaintext file. The test passes whether or not the snapshot is encrypted. Make it search raw and base64, and give it a positive control on a plaintext store that must find the marker. Read at 82efd5c. Acceptance: the test fails when the engine is removed from the config

test: no graphdb test proves that an encrypted store writes no plaintext anywhere. Add one that writes a random marker as a property value, label, property key, edge type and edge value, closes the store (and separately leaves it unclosed, as a crash), walks every file under the data directory and searches each for every marker in raw and base64 form, with a positive control on an unencrypted store that must find them. Cover UseMmapSnapshot=false with EnableBatching and EnableCompression too (not probed yet), and document the files that are plaintext by design (the edge store under UseDiskBackedEdges holds the graph shape; the WAL keeps LSN and op type). mapper-6b offers its own marker test, which already searches raw and base64, as a consumer contract; consider tagging this test as that contract. Read at 82efd5c

query (v2.0, breaking): refuse a plain Cypher DELETE of a node that still has relationships, as openCypher does, unless the query says DETACH DELETE. Deprecated in the release after v1.6.0 (user decision 2026-10-08, option C): 1.x keeps removing the relationships and reports query.Notice code plain-delete-detach in ResultSet.Notices and the REST header X-Cypher-Deprecation. For v2.0: check every node to delete before any delete, so a refused query changes nothing; the error names the node and says to use DETACH DELETE; remove the notice and header for this code; update the CHANGELOG Removed entry and docs/STABILITY_POLICY.md deprecation record. Check the deprecation log lines and consumers (syntopica-timer-spec uses DETACH DELETE for nodes) before shipping. Acceptance: plain DELETE of a connected node errors and leaves node and relationships in place, DELETE r, a with all relationships bound still works, seen red first

query: Cypher CREATE and MERGE are not per row and do not reuse bound variables. CreateStep.createNodes (pkg/query/executor_steps.go) creates a node for every node in the pattern, including a variable MATCH already bound, and binds it into every row; createRelationships reads only ctx.results[0] and does not bind the relationship variable. Probed 2026-10-08 at fce5328: MATCH (a:P {name:'x'}) CREATE (a)-[:R]->(b:Q) made a new unlabeled node and used it as a (the matched a was ignored); MATCH (a:P) CREATE (a)-[:R]->(b:Q) over 2 matches made 1 Q and 1 edge plus the stray node. MergeStep is also not per row: if any row matches, rows without a match are dropped and nothing is created for them. Fix: per row, reuse a bound node, create only unbound ones, bind the new relationship variable; MERGE per row. Carries syntopica-timer-spec's trust-cluster query (two relationship MERGEs with bound endpoints, run twice, idempotent): scratchpad syntopica_merge_test.go.keep from the multiple-match-clauses PR. Check consumers' MATCH ... CREATE (a)-[...]->(b) queries before shipping, since their data may already hold stray nodes. Acceptance: each probe gives the openCypher result, seen red first

storage: with EnableBatching true, a FlushInterval of 0 (or less) panics at open: BatchedWAL.backgroundFlusher calls time.NewTicker(bw.flushInterval) (pkg/wal/batched_wal.go:152) and storage passes config.FlushInterval with no check. Verified by a probe on fce5328. Refuse a non-positive FlushInterval (and a non-positive BatchSize, if it misbehaves the same way) at open with a typed config error naming the field. Asked by mapper-6b. Acceptance: open with FlushInterval 0 returns the error and leaves no goroutine, seen red first

storage: an mmap Close builds the whole snapshot in memory before writing it: it clones every overlay record, decodes the base records, sorts both lists, and builds adjacency maps and the membership index (pkg/storage/mmap_snapshot_persist.go:26-96, mmap_snapshot_writer.go:104-177; read at fce5328). A probe with 200,000 nodes and 199,999 edges raised HeapAlloc from 188 MiB to a 487 MiB peak, about 0.75 KB per record. On a consultant laptop (mapper-6b, 585,000 records) that is an estimated +440 MiB at Close. Design first: a streaming or two-pass writer that keeps only IDs and offsets, measured with TMPDIR on a real disk; the format must not change without a version bump

storage: ForEachNode (pkg/storage/node_operations.go:947, read at fce5328) visits every tenant's nodes and holds gs.mu.RLock while the callback runs, so a callback blocks every writer and a write inside it deadlocks. GetEdgesByTypeForTenant (tenant_operations.go:192) skips a damaged record with no report. Add a tenant-scoped iterator that does not hold the global lock across the callback (the paged readers NodesByLabelPageForTenant/EdgesByTypePageForTenant are the model), document or deprecate the tenant-blind form, and make the bulk readers report a damaged record (ADR 0003 enumeration rule). Found answering mapper-6b. Acceptance: a write inside the new iterator's callback does not deadlock; a damaged record surfaces as an error, seen red first

licensing: TelemetryReporter.Stop (pkg/licensing/telemetry.go:83) only cancels the context and does not wait for reportLoop, so a report already in flight can arrive after Stop returns. TestTelemetryReporter_reportLoop_Cancellation caught it once under make test-local load on 2026-10-08 (passes alone); the test also reads callCount from the handler goroutine without synchronisation. Make Stop wait for the loop (WaitGroup) and make the test's counter atomic. Acceptance: the test passes under -race -count=200, and fails with the wait removed

query: an aggregate inside WITH is not computed: WITH n.city AS city, count(n) AS c RETURN city, c does not group or count (found by the #657 review; the WITH projection in pkg/query/executor.go builds each row from one binding). Apply the implicit-grouping rule from v1.4-cypher-implicit-grouping to WITH: the non-aggregate items are the keys. Read at f9d28ed. Acceptance: the query above returns one row per city with its count, seen red first

query: WITH x AS y binds y to nil when the query never defined x (pkg/query/executor.go, the WITH projection copies binding.bindings[name] with no presence check), so a misspelled name after WITH matches nothing and writes nothing with no error; after #657 a null-bound variable matches nothing. Refuse an undefined variable in WITH the way DELETE, SET and REMOVE now do. Read at f9d28ed. Acceptance: WITH of an undefined variable errors, WITH of an OPTIONAL MATCH null still passes null, seen red first

storage + query: a property index on a float key may disagree with the scan for NaN and for -0 versus 0: the index keys on the encoded bytes while the scan compares numerically (raised in the #641 review, not checked). Probe first: index on a float property holding 0.0, -0.0 and NaN, then compare MATCH with and without the index for each value, using the #641 oracle (pkg/query/optimizer_index_oracle_test.go). If they differ, make the index path agree with the scan or keep such values off the index path. Not yet confirmed

encryption: encryption.Engine copies the key into masterKey and has no Close, Destroy or Zero method (pkg/encryption/engine.go), and GraphStorage.Close does not touch the engine, so the key stays in memory for the life of the process (found by the encryption review for mapper-6b, which stores client data on laptops). Add a method that zeroes the key and makes the engine refuse further use, and call it from GraphStorage.Close when the store owns the engine. Go cannot guarantee no other copy exists (GC moves, string conversions); document that limit. Read at f9d28ed

storage: snapshotWithBoundary takes gs.mu.RLock (pkg/storage/persistence.go) and releases it by hand, once on the JSON path and on three paths inside snapshotMmapLocked (mmap_snapshot_persist.go), so the lock is owned by two functions. A panic while it is held, for example decodeNodeRecordAt on an out-of-range mmap record (mmap is the default), leaves the read lock held: every later write and Close then waits forever. #665 made the other 37 sites panic-safe and left this one out. Proposed: one captureSnapshotState method takes the RLock with defer, calls panicPoint, reads the boundary and collects the mmap or JSON state; snapshotMmapLocked stops touching the lock; encode, rename and dir sync stay off-lock. Benchmark the RLock hold time before and after. Acceptance: a TestLockPanic_ case for the capture site, seen red first. Read at 2834586

api: POST /nodes/batch called CreateNodeWithTenant (pkg/api/handlers_nodes.go:373), so it skipped the uniqueness-rules registry (ADR 0001) that POST /nodes and GraphQL enforce, and stored a duplicate for every item that repeated a registered key, with created counting it as a success. graphdb-coord's claim_for_task rule is one such key. Route each item through CreateNodeWithUniquenessRulesForTenant and report a refusal as a batch item error, keeping the partial-success shape (CC7, CC20) and the R4 rule that no response names a rule. Acceptance: a batch with a duplicate of a stored key, a duplicate inside the batch and an item missing the rule property stores one node per key, seen red first. Read at d08c106

query: Cypher CREATE (pkg/query/executor_steps.go:304) and the MERGE create path (pkg/query/physical_ops_mutate.go:69, :360) call CreateNodeWithTenant, so a /query write skips the uniqueness-rules registry (ADR 0001) and stores a duplicate of a registered key with no error. ADR 0001 names two enforcement surfaces (GraphQL, REST create) and did not consider Cypher. Route Cypher node creation through CreateNodeWithUniquenessRulesForTenant, and decide how a refusal reaches the caller: an execution error that stops the query, with the rows already written in the same query documented (Cypher writes are not transactional here). MERGE matches first and then creates, so two concurrent MERGEs of one key can both create; the registry closes that race only if the create goes through it. Acceptance: CREATE of a duplicate key fails, concurrent MERGE of one key stores one node, seen red first. Read at d08c106

storage,api: PatchNodeForTenant and UpdateNodeForTenant (pkg/storage/node_operations.go:544, :568; REST PUT /nodes/{id}) never consult the uniqueness-rules registry (ADR 0001), so an update can set a rule's property to a value another node of that label already holds, and the store then has two holders of one key with no error. Found by the builder check of SPEC_node_upsert_2026-10-21.md (D6), which closes the same gap for the upsert merge only. Under the same gs.mu hold as the patch, check every registered rule whose label is on the node and whose property the patch changes, and refuse with *UniqueConstraintError (REST 409 with conflicting_node_id). Acceptance: a PUT that sets a held key value is refused and leaves the node unchanged, seen red first. Read at d08c106

storage: the storage Batch (pkg/storage/batch_executor.go, executeOps and executeUpdateNode near :179) and Transaction.Commit (pkg/storage/transaction_commit.go, writeTxNodeUpdate near :223; creates buffered in transaction_ops.go) never consult the uniqueness-rules registry (ADR 0001), on create or on update, so an embedded caller that uses either can store a duplicate of a registered key with no error. Every REST, GraphQL and Cypher write path enforces the registry after #674, #680 and #685; these two embedded-API paths are what is left (found by the #685 worker). Decide the refusal shape: the Batch keeps earlier ops on an error (v1.4-storage-batch-atomic-commit), a Transaction should refuse the whole commit. Acceptance: a Batch or Transaction create or update of a held key value is refused, seen red first. Read at 6b9b7a6

query: StreamingQuery.StreamNodes (pkg/query/stream_query.go, near :29) scans node IDs 1..GetStatistics().NodeCount and calls GetNode on each, so after a delete leaves an ID gap it skips the nodes whose IDs exceed the live count, and a store whose IDs do not start at 1 streams too few with no error. Enumerate the live nodes instead (the way ClusteringCoefficient does). Acceptance: create 3 nodes, delete the first, and StreamNodes returns the other 2, seen red first. Read at 108a6c4

api: the plain POST /nodes/batch reports a WAL append failure as the raw storage error text, because batchCreateItemError (pkg/api/handlers_nodes.go, near :249) falls through to err.Error() for ErrWALWriteFailed, so the wrapped disk error leaves the server. The merge batch (batchUpsertItemError, handlers_nodes_upsert.go near :172) already maps it to walWriteFailedMessage and logs it. Map it the same way in batchCreateItemError. Acceptance: a batch create item whose WAL append fails reports walWriteFailedMessage and no disk path, seen red first. Read at 108a6c4

api: the single upsert's WAL-failure path (respondUpsertWALWriteFailed, pkg/api/handlers_nodes_upsert.go near :110, answering 202 with the NodeNotDurableResponse fields plus created) has no test, and handlers_wal_write_error_test.go covers no upsert or batch route. Add a test with a failing WAL for POST /nodes?on_conflict=merge on the create and the merge branch, asserting 202, created, and the node. Acceptance: the test fails if the handler answers 500 or drops created (prove it by a revert). Read at 108a6c4

ci: the go-client workflow (.github/workflows/go-client.yml) runs gofmt, vet, build and test but no golangci-lint, and the root lint.yml does not reach the clients/go module, so lint findings in the client never fail CI (two errcheck findings found by hand in #684). Add a golangci-lint v2.13.2 step with working-directory clients/go, and gofmt -s in place of gofmt -l. Acceptance: a deliberate unchecked error in clients/go fails the new step on a test branch. Read at 108a6c4

go-client: Nodes.BatchCreate (clients/go/nodes.go:86) and the traverse helper (clients/go/helpers.go:34) end with `return out.Nodes, json.Unmarshal(res.data, &out)`. The Go spec does not fix the order of the out.Nodes read against the Unmarshal call, so a compiler may return the empty slice; gc happens to return the decoded one. Decode first, then return. Acceptance: no return in clients/go reads a variable that a call in the same return statement writes (grep check), and both methods keep their tests green. Read at 108a6c4

storage: CreateNodeWithTenant plans a vector insert under gs.mu and runs it after the unlock (applyNodeVectorInserts, pkg/storage/vector_operations.go near :381). A DeleteAllNodes in that window empties the HNSW index (VectorIndex.clearAll, #714), then the late insert puts the deleted node's vector into the new index, so VectorSearch can return an ID that does not exist. Batch, transaction commit and node upsert share the window. Needs an epoch check or a lock change. Acceptance: a concurrent create-and-clear test leaves CheckInvariants clean, seen red first. Read at 53c5cc1 plus #714

storage: DeleteAllNodes drops every property index definition (gs.propertyIndexes = make, clearAllUnderLock in pkg/storage/node_operations.go) but since #714 keeps vector index definitions, so a reload finds its vector indexes and silently loses its property indexes. Decide one rule for both, then make the clear keep each property index and empty its buckets, or drop both. Acceptance: after DeleteAllNodes and a repopulate, a property-index lookup behaves per the chosen rule, seen red first. Read at 53c5cc1 plus #714

storage: clearAllUnderLock (pkg/storage/node_operations.go) does not touch gs.edgeStore, so with UseDiskBackedEdges the LSM edge store may keep every edge after DeleteAllNodes. Untested: write a probe first. If edges survive, clear the edge store under the same lock. Acceptance: with UseDiskBackedEdges, GetEdge and the adjacency lookups find no pre-clear edge after DeleteAllNodes, and the probe is seen red first if the defect is real. Read at 53c5cc1

storage: an encrypted store that holds no ciphertext cannot prove a key at open. With a version 1 rules.json, no snapshot and no WAL, an open with a wrong key succeeds (a missing snapshot is a fresh database, pkg/storage/storage.go near :231), its Close writes snapshot.json under that key (snapshotWithBoundary, persistence.go near :561), and the next open with the right key fails with failed to decrypt snapshot: authentication failed. Design a key-check artefact (for example a small sealed file written at the first encrypted open and checked before any write). Acceptance: TestProbe_WrongKeyOpenThenCloseLocksOutRightKey (#721) loses its t.Skip and passes, and a format version is recorded. Read at 7a17414

test: TestEncryptedStore_WritesNoPlaintext/json-batching-compression/crash (pkg/storage/encryption_no_plaintext_test.go, #709) fails in about 2.5 percent of runs, 5 of 200 on main at 1ddd131. Each failure is the plaintext control at :213: the edgePropertyKey or edgePropertyValue marker is not on disk at the crash point, so the test cannot prove its search works. Find why the batched compressed WAL sometimes has no edge record at the crash point, then make the control deterministic. Acceptance: 1000 runs with -count=1000 pass, and the control can still fail when the marker is absent. Read at 1ddd131
query: MATCH (p:Person {id: 0}) WITH p.age AS age RETURN age names the result column age. with a trailing dot. Found by the Relate spike on 9eef8e1; row in pkg/queryutil/cypher_known_gaps_test.go
query: CALL algo.nope() through the server executor path answers affected=1 with no error. An unknown procedure must be refused by name. Row in pkg/queryutil/cypher_known_gaps_test.go
query: CALL algo.pageRank() with no YIELD answers affected=1 and no scores column, so the procedure result never reaches the caller. Row in pkg/queryutil/cypher_known_gaps_test.go

query: CALL algo.pageRank() YIELD scores RETURN scores returns a column named scores. with a null value, and YIELD of a column the procedure does not have (nodeId) is null instead of an error. Row in pkg/queryutil/cypher_known_gaps_test.go
query: MATCH (p:Person) RETURN q.name returns null for a variable the query never bound. Refuse it and name the variable; the WITH half is v1.4-cypher-with-undefined-variable
query: RETURN nosuchfn(1) AS x returns null with no error. An unknown function must be refused by name
query: RETURN range(1,3) AS r returns null; range() should build the list, step argument included

query: RETURN 1 / 0 and a string plus an integer both return null with no error. Decided 2026-11-12: refuse both, after scripts/consumer-drive.sh shows no consumer relies on the null. Needs a spec of the rule per operator
query: count(*) is a parser error (unexpected token in expression); it should equal count of the matched rows
query: count(DISTINCT x) is a parser error (unexpected token in expression)
query: UNWIND [1,2,3] AS x is refused (UNWIND expression must be a property reference); accept a list literal and a list parameter
query: a negative number in a pattern property map, MATCH (p:Person {id: -1}), is a parser error (expected value); the same literal in WHERE parses
query: a named path (MATCH p = ...), length(p) and shortestPath((a)-[:R*]-(b)) are parser errors. Needs a design before code
query: CALL { } subqueries, EXISTS { } subqueries and list comprehensions are parser or lexer errors. One design, one PR per form
query: a parser error prints a raw token number, e.g. unexpected token in expression: Token(54), with no token text and no column. Print the token text, line and column
query: add one corrective hint sentence to the refusals an agent hits most (unknown procedure, undefined variable, unknown function, unsupported clause), as Relate does
api: POST /query has no row limit and no truncated flag; a no-LIMIT scan returned 100000 rows. Add an opt-in limit, off by default, and a truncated field in the response. Check make contract-guard

storage: an mmap store with 10000 64-dim vectors took 11.7 to 17.3 s to open (4 runs, btrfs NVMe, warm cache); the same graph without vectors opened in 2 ms. Measure open time against vector count first, then choose: persist the HNSW index (format bump), lazy build, or parallel build
query: a three-hop cycle MATCH (a)-[:KNOWS]->(b)-[:KNOWS]->(c)-[:KNOWS]->(a) WHERE a.id = 42 took 17.8 s on 100k nodes and 500k edges (correct answer). Profile before any change

query: compareValues (pkg/query/ast_eval.go) returns 0 for two types it does not know, so WHERE p.nosuch >= 0 returns every node, WHERE p.city >= 1 on a string returns every row, WHERE p.flag < true returns none, and a Go int never differs from an int64. Null and mismatched types must not compare as equal

query: parseReturnItem keeps an aggregate argument only when it is a property or a variable, so RETURN collect(1) answers [] and sum(1) answers 0, and the executor cannot tell count(1) from count(null). Keep the argument expression in the AST; WITH already refuses these

query: the WITH ... WHERE filter in executeWithChain drops a row when the expression returns an error (if err != nil { continue }), so WITH p.age AS age, count(p) AS c WHERE c IN 5 answers 0 rows and no error
query: SKIP and LIMIT written after WITH apply to the final result, not to the WITH: MATCH (p:Person) WITH p LIMIT 1 MATCH (q:Person) RETURN q.id answered 1 row where openCypher answers 6

query: CallStep checks a YIELD name against the bound variables of the input rows, so with zero input rows MATCH (scores:NoSuch) CALL algo.pageRank() YIELD scores raises nothing. Check against the pattern variables of the AST instead

query: an unbound variable as a procedure argument becomes nil and algo.labelPropagation and algo.eMeans then run with defaults; parseCall makes the comma between arguments optional (CALL algo.kHop(1 1) runs); 1e308 lexes as two arguments

query: algo.pageRank, kHop, shortestPath, nodeSimilarity, linkPrediction and detectCycles discard their context, so one procedure call cannot stop at the query timeout, and maxIterations has no cap. Pass ctx into the algorithms and check it per iteration

api: respondJSON writes the status line before it encodes the body, so a value encoding/json refuses (for example -Inf) answers HTTP 200 with an empty body. Encode into a buffer first and answer 500 on failure
query: EXPLAIN CALL algo.nope() succeeds and shows step:Unknown, because CallStep has no step name or detail and EXPLAIN does not look the procedure up
query: RegisterProcedure writes procedureRegistry with no lock, and CALL now reads that map on every request

query: = and <> of plain values are two-valued: p.nosuch <> 1 and p.s <> 1 return every row and null = null is true, where openCypher gives null and drops the row. Only = and <> over an unknown comparison are three-valued (pkg/query/three_valued.go). Changes many queries; needs a changelog entry

query: MATCH (p {id: $v}) with a JSON number (float64) does not find an int64 property, because the pattern map uses MatchStep.valuesEqual (match_helpers.go), and MERGE (p:M {id: $v}) then creates a duplicate node
query: with a property index, WHERE p.age = 40 does not return the node that holds 40.0; the scan path returns it. The index lookup and the scan must agree

query: the ORDER BY comparator returns 0 for a null or for types with no common order, so it is not a strict weak order and [2, null, 1] sorts to different results for different input orders. Give null and mixed types a fixed place, as openCypher does
query: MIN and MAX over mixed types or NaN depend on the row order: ['a', 1] gives min a and max a, [1, 'a'] gives 1 and 1
query: sum adds a plain Go int but avg does not count it (isSummed in aggregation_functions.go), so avg of int 1 and int64 4 is 5, not 2.5. A plain int comes from COUNT and from procedure columns

graphql: compareNumeric (pkg/graphql/filtering_eval.go) returns 0 for a value that is not a number, so gte and lte are true for a string or a boolean against a number, and a string gte a string is always true

query: WHERE p.flag with no operator returns no rows, because Eval of a bare property is an error and the lenient filter drops the row; NOT of a function that returns null still coerces to true. Route a bare condition and function results through evalTri
query: coalesce(), exists() and the other common openCypher functions are not registered; they gave null and are now refused as unknown. Add coalesce first
query: GetFunction matches a function name exactly, though its comment says case-insensitive, so toupper() and TOUPPER() are refused. openCypher function names are case-insensitive
query: extractValue (pkg/query/ast_eval.go) discards the error a function returns and gives null, so range(1,3,$step) with step 0 and size(range(0, p.id*1000000)) answer null or 0 with no error

query: PropertyExpression and FunctionCallExpression hold no line and column, so undefined variable and unknown function errors have no position and are not a SyntaxError. Add the position in parsePrimaryExpression

query: the undefined-variable check uses one name set per segment, so MATCH (a) WHERE b.x = 1 CREATE (b) is accepted and answers 0 rows; a name in WHERE before a bare CALL and a CALL argument that names its own YIELD column also pass
query: checkQueryNames adds about 1 microsecond and 4 to 5 allocations per query (RETURN 1: 1559 ns to 1822 ns); bindSegment and orderScope build maps per segment
query: MATCH ()-[:KNOWS]->(b) RETURN b answers 0 rows; an anonymous start node does not match
query: RETURN DISTINCT p.city AS c ORDER BY p.id answers one row per node, because the injected sort column makes each row distinct
api: an error a procedure returns for its arguments (algo.kHop: sourceID must be a numeric node ID) is not a RefusalError, so POST /query answers 500 and hides the text
query: resolveParameters in pkg/query/executor.go does not replace a parameter in an OPTIONAL MATCH pattern, so OPTIONAL MATCH (p {id: $v}) binds null in silence for each parameter type
query: a stored integer above 2^53 and a float parameter compare as equal in WHERE and in a pattern map, because compareOrdered converts the integer to float64

query: a query can refuse on a scan and return rows when an index selects fewer nodes, for example MATCH (p:T) WHERE p.q AND p.id = 1 RETURN p.id where another node holds a string in q. The index path in pkg/query/optimizer.go never reads the other node. The same query must give the same answer for both plans
query: an ORDER BY expression is never evaluated. RETURN p.name ORDER BY p.age / 0 does not refuse, and an ORDER BY expression does not sort
query: the executor has no rollback, so a query that writes and then refuses keeps its writes and answers 400. Needs a design
query: [1] + [2] and p.nums + [3] are valid openCypher and are refused as not supported
query: [1, null] = [1, null] is true and null IN [1] and 1 IN [null] are false, where openCypher gives null (TCK Comparison1 scenario 6 and 7, List5 scenario 20 to 41)

query: WITH 1 AS p MATCH (p:T) WHERE p.pid = 1 SET p.z = 1 binds p again to each matching node and writes them, where openCypher refuses a MATCH of a variable that holds a value that is not a node (matchNode in pkg/query/match_node.go falls through to the scan). Same result with and without an index

query: VectorSearchStep selects the top-k nodes before the WHERE filter runs, so a refusal on a row it hides depends on a vector index. The plan-independence rules of evalPredicate do not cover it, because the vector step does not run the other conjuncts

query: EXPLAIN of a UNION runs the second part, because executeUnion runs each later part under EXPLAIN. It must return a plan for each part and run no step. EXPLAIN of a UNION also keeps the missing-parameter check for this reason

query: ExecuteWithText runs the first segment only: a write after WITH answers affected=N and writes nothing, and a UNION returns the rows of its first part. QueryCache.Get and Put also race on the cache map from many goroutines, and the cached plan is not dropped when an index is created or removed. Only cmd/integration-test calls it: make it use the normal path or remove it

storage: createLiveNodeLocked stores the properties map and the labels slice of the caller in the live node with no copy and no documented ownership rule, so a caller that changes its map after CreateNode changes the stored node outside the lock and the WAL, and a later SET changes the map of the caller. Copy on create, or document that the store takes ownership, with a measured cost for the bulk path

query: the parser refuses a list literal inside a list literal (invalid list element: expected value, got '['), which blocks 27 of the 37 scenarios of TCK List5 at the query level. The 27 scenarios are skipped rows in pkg/query/equality_collections_test.go, and TestInTri_SkipListIsHonest fails when one starts to parse
query: WITH ... ORDER BY does not parse (unexpected token ORDER), with SKIP and LIMIT after it. No scenario of TCK WithOrderBy1 to WithOrderBy4 runs (292 scenarios)

query: ORDER BY max(x) and ORDER BY count(n) are refused (an aggregate works only as a whole RETURN or WITH item), and RETURN c.city, count(p) AS c ORDER BY c * -1 is refused as an expression after an aggregate. TCK ReturnOrderBy2 scenario 3 and ReturnOrderBy6 scenario 1 need the first form

query: a parameter costs one map entry in each row that enters a segment, so a WITH chain on 100,000 rows takes about 17 percent more time with a parameter than with a literal, with equal allocations. Replace each ParameterExpression with a literal in the copy of the query that each run already makes for patterns, so no row holds a $name key

query: SET p.t = [$a, 2] through POST /query stores a general JSON list, where the literal [1, 2] stores an integer list, because JSON gives each number as a float64 and the list then holds mixed number types. Decide the stored type of a list of mixed JSON numbers and add a test

query: extractIndexableCondition returns the first equality of the AND chain, so WHERE p.k = 1 AND p.pid = 1 does not use an index on pid when k has none. Costs speed only: try each equality of the chain

test: make the openCypher TCK feature files the source of TestCypherKnownGaps. A harness that runs each scenario and records parse-and-pass, parse-and-fail and no-parse gave, on 2026-11-13: ReturnOrderBy2 to 6, 4 of 23 pass; WithOrderBy1 to 4, 0 of 292 run; List5, 10 of 37 run as query text. Commit the harness and the counts so that each parser fix moves a measured number
